first.rationale: Referral incentives have the strongest inherited evidence for adding qualified revenue without measurable retention harm. Verifying that result and the retention damage from promotional pricing will test the key sustainable-growth tradeoff before committing; target established customers rather than reacting to competitor pricing with broad discounts.

final.rationale: Run a referral-incentive experiment limited to established accounts older than six months. The verified evidence shows a 21% increase in referral starts, 7% growth in qualified revenue, and 2% higher 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower retention and failure at first renewal. Keep the test segment-specific because the referral effect was concentrated in mature accounts.
